key_insight: A DFT-trained machine-learning potential can efficiently predict thermophysical properties and phase behavior of NaCl–KCl mixtures across compositions and temperatures, though some absolute values remain biased.
engineering_relevance: This enables large-scale molecular dynamics screening of molten salt systems for heat-transfer and materials design, while still requiring experimental calibration for high-confidence deployment.
method: Trained a moment tensor potential on DFT data for NaCl, KCl, NaCl–KCl mixtures, and NaK alloy.
Tested the impact of D3 dispersion corrections on model behavior.
Used the potential in large-scale MD to predict density, diffusion, RDFs, heat capacity, thermal conductivity, and the NaCl–KCl phase diagram.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports systematic evaluation across wide temperature and composition ranges and finds that the model reproduces many trends but not all absolute property values.
watch_item: The potential shows systematic deviations in several properties, so experimental validation is still needed before relying on it for quantitative engineering decisions.
paper_title: Machine-Learning Potentials for sodium-potassium chloride mixtures: Predicting thermophysical properties and phase behavior of multicomponent salts
